jobs_results.description:
Who We Are Looking For

State Street is seeking a Cryptographic Agility & Post-Quantum (PQC) Engineer to help shape and deliver the firm's enterprise cryptographic modernization strategy. This role is ideal for a cybersecurity professional with a strong foundation in cryptography, encryption technologies, and security engineering who is passionate about preparing the organization for emerging cryptographic threats, including the impact of quantum computing.

The successful candidate will partner across cybersecurity, architecture, engineering, infrastructure, and application teams to establish and operationalize a formal cryptographic agility capability. You will help ensure the organization can efficiently identify cryptographic dependencies, evaluate emerging standards, and execute controlled transitions to new cryptographic algorithms while maintaining security, compliance, and business continuity.

What You Will Be Responsible For

As a Cryptographic Agility & PQC Engineer, you will:

Mature the enterprise Cryptographic Agility program, enabling the organization to respond effectively to evolving cryptographic risks and industry standards.Develop and maintain an inventory of cryptographic assets, dependencies, algorithms, protocols, certificates, keys, and related technologies across applications, platforms, and infrastructure.Identify systems utilizing vulnerable, deprecated, or legacy cryptographic algorithms and define remediation and migration strategies.Evaluate emerging post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards and technologies, with a focus on NIST-approved cryptographic algorithms and industry best practices.Define approved cryptographic migration paths, transition frameworks, and implementation guidance for application and platform teams.Partner with enterprise architecture, platform engineering, application development, PKI, and infrastructure teams to assess cryptographic readiness and capabilities.Pilot and validate PQC-enabled technologies, services, and solutions to support future enterprise adoption.Develop standards, procedures, and technical guidance supporting cryptographic agility and quantum readiness initiatives.Monitor changes in the cryptographic landscape, including advancements in quantum computing, regulatory expectations, and industry standards.Produce metrics, dashboards, and executive reporting to track cryptographic risk, migration progress, and PQC readiness across the enterprise.Contribute to strategic security initiatives focused on strengthening the organization's long-term cryptographic resilience.


What We Value

Understanding of modern cryptographic concepts, encryption technologies, PKI, certificate management, and key management systems.Experience assessing security risks and translating technical findings into actionable remediation plans.Ability to collaborate effectively across diverse technology and business teams to drive enterprise-wide initiatives.Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a structured approach to complex technical challenges.Curiosity and a desire to stay current with advancements in cybersecurity, cryptography, and quantum computing.Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.A proactive mindset focused on continuous improvement, operational excellence, and risk reduction.Experience working within highly regulated financial services or other complex enterprise environments is a plus.


Required Qualifications

Education & Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related discipline, or equivalent work experience.5+ years of experience in cybersecurity, security engineering, encryption, PKI, key management, infrastructure security, or a related field.Working knowledge of cryptographic algorithms, protocols, and security controls used in enterprise environments.Experience with enterprise operating systems, cloud platforms, and distributed application architectures.Familiarity with cloud platforms such as AWS, Microsoft Azure, OCI, or Google Cloud Platform.Exposure to post-quantum cryptography concepts, cryptographic inventory/discovery tools, or cryptographic risk assessments.Experience supporting security compliance frameworks, cybersecurity standards, and audit activities.Experience developing scripts or automation solutions using languages such as Python, PowerShell, Bash, Java, C#, or Go.Experience with infrastructure-as-code and automation frameworks such as Terraform, Ansible, Jenkins, Harness, or similar CI/CD platforms.Industry certifications such as CISSP, Certified Encryption Specialist (ECES), or similar certifications are desirable.


Salary Range

$120,000 - $202,500 Annual

The range quoted above applies to the role in the primary location specified. If the candidate would ultimately work outside of the primary location above, the applicable range could differ.

Description


Quantum Sky is seeking a Principal Solutions Architect to drive the technical execution of our Post-Quantum Cryptography offerings. This role bridges strategy and delivery - translating customer requirements and organizational roadmaps into actionable engineering backlogs, driving business development through proposal responses and product demonstrations, and directly advising customers on their cryptographic transition and migration planning. Ability to help build actionable PQC migration roadmaps and action plans tailored to their environment and risk tolerance.


Responsibilities:




Partner with the Director to guide development teams in building out PQC product offerings.




Translate customer and market requirements into well-defined epics, user stories, and a prioritized development backlog.




Provide technical oversight to ensure implementations align with NIST PQC standards and sound cryptographic engineering practice.




Contribute technical and market insight to inform PQC offering strategy and roadmap.




Contribute technical responses including solution architecture to BAAs, RFIs, and RFPs.




Guide customers through PQC transition and migration planning, including cryptographic inventory, risk prioritization, phased migration roadmaps and action plans, orchestration, implementation, and continuous monitoring.




Assess and communicate cryptographic and key management risk




Advise on prioritization frameworks for migration based on data sensitivity, system criticality, and crypto-agility.




Qualifications


Required:




Advanced Academic Background: BS/MS in Cryptography, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related field, with a solid working understanding of cryptographic and PQC algorithms.




Federal Cyber Experience: 3+ years of experience in federal cybersecurity, including direct involvement in NSA/NIST pilots.




Cryptographic Engineering: 5+ years of experience in encryption/secure systems engineering, PKI, and key management solutions, including 2-3 years of hands-on involvement in PQC migration planning or implementation.




PQC Knowledge: Working knowledge of NIST PQC algorithms (e.g., ML-KEM, ML-DSA) and how key material is generated, distributed, and consumed within cryptographic systems and cryptonets.




Communication: Demonstrated ability to communicate technical cryptographic concepts to both engineering teams and executive/business audiences, and to operate effectively across customer organizational levels.




Strategic Partnering: Proven ability to curate and manage partners for inventorying, distributed key management, software-defined cryptography, and quantum-resistant solutions.




Desired:




Experience with distributed key management architectures and crypto-inventory tooling.




Experience with PQC deployments or PQC implementations in constrained/tactical DoW/IC environments.




Familiarity with AI/ML applications in cyber operations or PQC migration tooling.




Prior experience developing roadmaps, maturity models, or migration playbooks.




Publications, conference talks, or community contributions in PQC and applied cryptography.




Clearance




No clearance required to apply.




Must be a U.S. citizen and eligible for TS/SCI.




Active security clearance is a plus.

US, Remote

Compensation is unique to each candidate and relative to the skills and experience they bring to the position. The salary range for this position is typically between $175,000-$215,000. Highlights of our benefits include Health/Dental/Vision, 401(k) match, Paid Time Off, STD/LTD/Life Insurance, Referral Bonuses, professional development reimbursement, and parental leave.
